name: Venetian nationalism
summary: Venetian nationalism (Venetism) holds that the Venetian people form a distinct nation with its own history, language and the legacy of the Republic of Venice, and should govern themselves, ranging from fiscal federalism and autonomy within Italy to full independence. It is a regionalist, pro-European and anti-Rome movement, strongly tied to keeping Veneto's tax revenue and cutting bureaucracy, and it spans left and right, with a centre-right Liga Veneta mainstream. It pursues its aims by referendums and councils, not violence, and its social and immigration positions are mixed.
scope: The mainstream Venetist movement from the Liga Veneta (founded 1979-80) to the 2012 Resolution 44, the Plebiscito.eu 2014 online referendum, the 2017 autonomy referendum and the 2012 Statute of Veneto. It excludes the wider Padanian/Lega Nord national programme and small radical groups such as the MLNV; the autonomist and independentist wings are blended and most social-issue answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Regional healthcare is a core devolved competence and the Zaia-era platforms stressed welfare and public-service reform, so support is inferred rather than documented.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Liga Veneta platforms stress low taxes and labour reform without a documented wage-floor line; its small-business base and welfare rhetoric pull opposite ways.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The party's priorities of low taxes and less bureaucracy imply market-friendliness, but it is a catch-all party with no stated market doctrine.

public-ownership.rationale: Platforms attack bureaucracy and heavy state burden; nothing in the sources favours nationalising industry, so mild opposition is inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The programme centres on lower taxes for Veneto's productive base; higher taxes on the wealthy are not part of it.

unions-good.rationale: The sources do not discuss unions; adherents range from small-business owners to left Venetists, so the movement is split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Low-tax, anti-bureaucracy positions of a small-owner region suggest respect for property, though this is inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Venetists object to bureaucracy more than to corporations; the sources show no line either way.

cut-welfare.rationale: Platforms under Zaia focused on welfare and public-service reform, and the 2025 platform stressed solidarity, so deep cuts are unlikely to be the adherent view.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nothing in Venetist programmes favours collective ownership; the small-business, low-tax orientation points against it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed by Venetist sources; adherents from libertarian-leaning founders to law-and-order Lega members are split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No documented stance; the Lega-linked mainstream tends towards conservative drug policy, though the founders were libertarian, so only a weak lean is inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The 2012 manifesto criticised xenophobic statements as damaging, but no legal restriction is documented, and libertarian roots pull the other way.

strong-leader.rationale: Venetism pursues autonomy by referendums and regional councils, a democratic route; a bypass-gridlock strongman is not part of it.

state-harmful.rationale: Venetists want a self-governing Venetian state or region, not no state; the 2012 Statute even affirms regional institutions.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented position; the movement lacks a stance and members are mixed.

empower-police-military.rationale: The sources show no line on police or military funding, and founders' libertarianism and later Lega law-and-order views conflict.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No documented position; the Catholic-leaning mainstream of the party suggests mild opposition.

decide-locally.rationale: Core demand is autonomy and self-government for Veneto from Rome, and Liga Veneta's founding slogan was to be farther from Rome.

rehabilitation.rationale: The sources are silent on penal policy, so the movement is treated as split.

traditional-family.rationale: The party is Catholic-influenced, and the 2025 platform stressed roots and identity, but it has also taken liberal end-of-life positions.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: No Venetist doctrine; the Lega-based mainstream is socially conservative, though the Zaia wing is more liberal.

abortion-legal.rationale: The Zaia wing is socially liberal on end-of-life care while the Catholic and Verona wings are conservative, so adherents are split.

more-religion-public.rationale: The founders were secular, while the 2025 platform is described as Christian-democratic; no single position is stated.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Race-conscious redress has no place in Venetist programmes; the focus on Venetian identity suggests mild disagreement.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; the culturally conservative mainstream is unlikely to endorse it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The regional Statute commits the Region to protecting the Venetian people's history, culture and language, and Venetists centre their movement on heritage. The Statute is regional law, not a nationalist text.

gradual-change.rationale: Venetists seek a sharp constitutional change (independence) by referendum but via legal and institutional channels, so the answer is mixed.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The 2010 platform called for integration and respect for diversity, while the Lega wing is restrictive, so adherents are divided.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The movement values a Europe of the regions but wants Veneto's own sovereignty; stronger UN powers are not discussed.

free-trade.rationale: Venetists are export-oriented, Europe-friendly and low-tax, and the 2014 poll asked about joining the EU and the euro.

nation-first.rationale: "We are a nation, Veneto is not Italy" frames a self-interested nation project, though Venetists remain pro-EU, so only mild agreement.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The independence poll included NATO membership, but no stance on human-rights interventions is documented.

open-borders.rationale: Integration is supported but no source endorses open borders; Venetists want their own border control.

limit-growth.rationale: Priorities are low taxes and a green economy, not degrowth; growth is valued by this export region.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The party promotes a green economy but opposes nuclear plants, and has no documented drastic-action line.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Liga Veneta opposes building nuclear power plants in Veneto.

revolution-justified.rationale: Venetists pursue referendums and legal petitions; those accused of plotting violence called themselves pacifists, and Zaia distanced himself from radical acts.

experts-over-public.rationale: Venetism leans on popular referendums over technocratic decision-making, so mild disagreement is inferred.

central-planning.rationale: The movement is anti-bureaucratic, low-tax and region-driven, and aimed at escaping central control from Rome.

socialized-markets.rationale: Venetism spans left and right parties, so adherents are split on worker or public ownership with markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not a Venetist proposal; the movement favours lowering taxes in general, not a single land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Small-family-business base and low-tax programme suggest opposition to heavy inheritance taxes.

basic-income.rationale: Not part of Venetist programmes; the focus on work, labour and low taxes suggests mild opposition.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Export-oriented Veneto and Europeanist platform point against tariffs, though no explicit stance is documented.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The anti-bureaucracy line suggests distrust of directed investment from Rome; regional development funding might be acceptable, so only mild disagreement.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Veneto's small-business economy and low-tax orientation are consistent with widely dispersed small ownership, though this is inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not on any Venetist platform; inferred from its market, low-tax, pro-business programmes.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The independence poll proposed joining the euro, implying acceptance of a central bank.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Nothing in the programmes points to state-recognised wage-setting bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Venetist parties compete across the whole ideological spectrum in elections and reject single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Venetists revere the Republic of Venice, which was an elective republic, not a hereditary monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Venetists pursue independence through referendums and regional democracy, and honour the Venetian Republic tradition.

direct-votes.rationale: Plebiscito.eu staged an online referendum and Venetists demand a vote on independence and autonomy.

workers-councils.rationale: Not a Venetist idea; the movement works through regional councils and parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: Independentist Venetism demands a right to self-determination and an independence referendum, as in Resolution 44/2012. The autonomist mainstream, as in the 2017 referendum, seeks more autonomy within Italy instead.

natural-rulers.rationale: The popular referendum approach and plain democratic orientation point against the view.

political-violence-never.rationale: Venetist mainstream and even the accused separatists said they were pacifists, though a radical fringe was prosecuted for plotting.

war-builds-character.rationale: No documented stance; the pro-Europe and pacifist-claiming movement points mildly against.

separate-church-state.rationale: The founders were secular but the later party drifts Christian-democratic, so adherents are divided.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the movement's secular or Christian-democratic character.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Founders were libertarian in outlook but nothing in the sources endorses private courts or defence.

military-superiority.rationale: An independent Veneto would join NATO per the poll, but military superiority is not addressed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Venetism defines the Venetian people by history, language and territory, not documented as ethnic purity, and the party stresses integration.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Venetists see Rome versus Veneto and the national question as the main conflict, not class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Programmes stress low taxes and work, not equalising outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed, though Venetists regard themselves as a distinct people with rights to their territory.

civilizational-union.rationale: Venetists favour a Europe of the regions, a broader union of peoples, but not a religious-civilisational one.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Venetist sources take no philosophical line on self-interest; the movement's fiscal grievances sit beside a Christian-democratic solidarity strand, so it is left neutral.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; party spans libertarian and Christian-democratic traditions.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed apart from a generic green-economy line.

limit-population.rationale: Nothing in the sources supports population limits; Venetists lament depopulation and emigration of the past.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Veneto is an industrial, export-focused region and its movement seeks prosperity, not rejection of industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No Venetist source discusses technological disruption; the region's industrial base and the localist heritage emphasis pull in opposite directions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bioenhancement never appears in Venetist programmes, and the liberal and Catholic wings of Liga Veneta would likely differ, so it is neutral.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Venetists value direct online voting, but nothing supports AI replacing political decision-making.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed by any Venetist source.

restore-past-order.rationale: Venetism invokes the Republic of Venice but aims at a modern federal state, so it is split between nostalgia and progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement is a catch-all spanning the whole spectrum and defines itself above left and right.

direct-action.rationale: Venetists use elections, councils and referendums; the violent plot allegations concerned a fringe.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not a Venetist idea; the movement is industrial and market-oriented.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from its conventional market programmes.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Venetist programmes reward work and enterprise and complain about funding the south.

production-for-use.rationale: Market, low-tax small-business economy is assumed.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from Venetism's pro-business base in small enterprise.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rejected by all main Venetist parties, which are electoral and democratic.

collective-farming.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from Veneto's economy of small owners.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a Venetist theme; the movement is pro-market and pro-EU.

taxation-theft.rationale: Venetists complain of high taxes and fiscal oppression (LIFE group) but do not call all taxation theft; split.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; founders were libertarian but later wings conservative.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Venetists claim a collective right of the Venetian people to self-government, which is a group right.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is not militarist, and conscription is unpopular in Italy since its abolition.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Secession is the exit idea, but Venetists also pursue voice through referendum and autonomy talks.

state-as-business.rationale: Anti-bureaucracy, efficiency framing might appeal, but it is not documented.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; the Statute's aim of removing imbalances is general.

media-academia-power.rationale: Venetists criticise Rome's political class but the sources do not single out universities or media, so no position is inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The 2012 manifesto criticised xenophobic statements and Veneto's mainstream stresses cultural, not racial, identity.

organic-representation.rationale: Venetists use party-based elections and regional councils.

total-state.rationale: The movement seeks less state control from Rome and fiscal autonomy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Calls to revive Venetian language and identity suggest rebirth, but the movement does not frame itself around decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Some Venetists advocate a larger Venetia including Friuli and parts of Lombardy, but the mainstream does not seek expansion by force.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the movement's democratic, autonomist programme.

bound-labor.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the movement's modern democratic programme.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; a mild lean against postmodern epistemology is inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic wing might agree, secular wing not.

single-common-good.rationale: The catch-all party style balances interests; no common-good doctrine is documented.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: About three million Venetians emigrated between 1870 and 1910, and Venetists maintain ties to the diaspora, so a return right is plausible.

revive-national-language.rationale: Veneto recognised Venetian as a regional language in 2007 and Venetists promote it, though not as sole state language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not on Venetist programmes; pro-business orientation suggests disagreement.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Low-tax, fiscally conservative framing of northern grievances suggests concern over deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Anti-bureaucracy, low-tax orientation points to agreement, though inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: The movement relies on elections, statutes and referendums; moral example of rulers as a substitute for law is never discussed.

national-self-determination.rationale: Most Venetists consider Veneto a nation distinct from Italy, and Resolution 44/2012 called for self-determination of the Venetian people.

force-without-un.rationale: The poll's NATO question shows alliance interest but no stance on force without the UN.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; secular founders and Catholic-leaning later wings conflict.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The 2010 platform urged integration of immigrants while the Lega wing reserves benefits for natives; adherents are split.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not documented; Zaia-era platforms reformed welfare but with no clear work requirement.

class-collaboration.rationale: The catch-all, small-business, regionalist movement stresses the whole Venetian community over class divisions.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Statute commits the Region to protecting cultural heritage, and Venetists prize Venice's inheritance.

dominated-front.rationale: Venetists see themselves as dominated by Rome, not by Western powers, and favour the EU and NATO.

workers-nation.rationale: The movement organises by territory and nation across classes, with workers' national orientation implicitly accepted.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not a Venetist demand; the party has liberal elements.

ban-interest.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the movement's pro-market outlook.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The 2012 manifesto criticised xenophobic statements, and mainstream Venetists have no racial-legal programme.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Venetists see the Italian state as a tool of Rome and the south more than of a class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The party stresses a green economy and opposes nuclear power; no fossil expansion is stated.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The 2010 platform called for integration but also respect for diversity, so a full assimilation demand is not uniformly held.

elite-replacement.rationale: The 2012 manifesto criticised xenophobic statements, and the replacement narrative is not documented as Venetist.

national-mission.rationale: Venetists seek self-rule for their own people, not to spread a model abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not Venetist doctrine; a mild lean against is inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Venetism is anti-Rome and condemns clientelism and bureaucracy in the capital, but this is not a fully populist programme.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the socially liberal Zaia wing.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Libertarian founders may agree, but the party also favours welfare and public services, so it is split.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not a Venetist idea; the 2012 manifesto rejected xenophobic statements.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Mainstream platforms call for respect for diversity and integration, supporting equal moral worth, though not stated in those terms.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not a Venetist question, though some left Venetists exist.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed, and Venetists themselves do not apply the colonial frame to states.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; the sources show no stance.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not documented; party is secular or Christian-democratic, with no conversion restrictions.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a Venetist idea; Veneto has a large cattle and meat industry.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The party's secular founders and Christian-democratic later wings split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not a Venetist question, and the movement opposes strong central states.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The claim that the 1866 plebiscite was invalid and the demand for a referendum rest on consent of the Venetian people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Veneto is a major exporter and the movement resents funding the south; a surplus orientation is inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: The 2012 manifesto rejected xenophobic statements and the movement is non-violent; not an element of Venetism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Venetists stress peaceful referendum routes and pacifism, but libertarian absolutism is not documented.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: No source addresses competition between peoples as progress; the Europeanist, market-leaning outlook gives only an uncertain pull.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed, though Italian law sanctions certain parties and Venetist groups faced prosecution.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The claim of domination by Rome and annexation in 1866 echoes non-domination, but isn't framed in those terms.

separated-powers.rationale: The Venetists respect constitutional court rulings and regional-council procedures, and the republic tradition had checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not a Venetist idea; parties operate in parliamentary politics.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The 2025 platform stressed solidarity, but the main focus is regional, so split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not documented; the small-owner outlook inclines to agreement but evidence is absent.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Venetist platforms discuss taxes and bureaucracy but never strike law, and the movement includes both business-minded and left-wing members.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The party's immigration approach is split between the integration platform and the Lega wing.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not a Venetist idea; electoral politics is assumed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Venetists have objected to prosecutions of separatists, suggesting wariness of suspended protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not documented; pro-market orientation suggests disagreement.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; split between integration platform and stricter Lega wing.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of elected officials is not a Venetist theme, though anti-Rome complaints about a costly political class might favour it; no source confirms.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the party is described as a catch-all without formal factions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Europeanism is central to Liga Veneta ("farther from Rome, closer to Europe", a Europe of the regions), and the 2014 poll asked about EU membership.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not a Venetist idea; regional government is parliamentary.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside Venetism's remit; the Catholic-leaning wing might accept bishops, the secular founders would not care.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not documented; a mild lean against is inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed, though Zaia held long regional presidency.

recall-officials.rationale: Venetists favour more direct citizen decision-making, so recall is plausible.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The 2014 poll asked about NATO membership, with support, implying alliance membership is accepted.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not documented; the movement disavows violence.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Venetism praises heritage and roots, but Veneto is heavily urbanised and industrial, and no source ranks rural over city life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Some Venetists seek a Venetia including Friuli-Venezia Giulia and parts of Lombardy, reuniting historic lands, but this is not universal.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; populist anti-elite rhetoric exists but this is not documented.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Venetism promotes its own culture but also respect for diversity, so split.

death-penalty.rationale: Not documented; Italy abolished it and mainstream platforms do not demand it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; secular and Catholic wings differ.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not documented; unlikely to be an adherent demand.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not a Venetist topic; the liberal Zaia wing and the conservative Verona wing of the party would differ.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed, though diaspora ties favour descent while the integration platform allows others.

minority-language-support.rationale: Veneto recognised Venetian as a regional language in 2007, and a 2016 act sought national minority status for Venetians; promotion of Venetian is central.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for minority religions are not discussed; the Catholic-majority identity politics and integration platform point in different directions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Venetism values local custom and heritage, but the libertarian founders valued individual freedom, so there is no clear line.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not documented; fiscally conservative framing suggests mild opposition.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Venetists see independence as primarily political and fiscal, keeping the market economy.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The movement proclaimed an independent Venetian Republic with a provisional parliament, which suggests support for founding a new constitution.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Venetists are democratic and reject authoritarian development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not documented; the movement complains of transfers to the south.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The 2014 poll proposed NATO membership, and no Venetist source seeks independent nuclear weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Venetists favour direct popular decisions; the region's president is directly elected.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The poll endorsed euro adoption, implying ECB independence is accepted, but nothing is documented.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Venetists have no external territorial conflict, and the question about land-for-peace deals has no counterpart in their programmes.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Venetist sources do not discuss the social function of property; libertarian founders and the Christian-democratic 2025 platform differ.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A dispute about the Soviet Union's character is irrelevant to Venetism, whose members range from left to right.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed beyond a generic green-economy platform.

collective-defense.rationale: The 2014 poll asked about NATO membership and found majority support among respondents.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Most Venetists say the 1866 annexation by plebiscite was invalid and held under military pressure, implying unlawful occupation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not documented; Venetists lean Catholic, so mild opposition.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Venetists do not discuss the head of state's role; Italy's president is an issue only as a symbol of the unity they contest.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Venetists claim self-determination and criticise suppression of independence referenda by the Constitutional Court and prosecutions.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Venetist demands since 2017 are for autonomy under Article 116 within Italy, and the Statute defines Veneto as autonomous within the Republic.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not documented; low-taxes stance but no flat-tax line.

character-from-environment.rationale: The nature-nurture question is never taken up in Venetist sources, so no position can be inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Not a Venetist idea; the movement relies on legal procedures.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy never appears in Venetist programmes, so the answer is a neutral placeholder rather than a stated view.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The Republic of Venice had a mixed constitution, but Venetists do not advance it as a doctrine.

leader-cult.rationale: Not documented; the movement is regional-democratic.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-law presumptions on shared custody are outside Venetist programmes; nothing in the sources decides it.

refugee-return.rationale: Venetists have no expelled-population grievance comparable to this, though 19th-century mass emigration is remembered; no source applies it to return rights.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Some Venetists claim a larger Venetia, but this is not a uniform or central position.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not a Venetist idea, though Lega-aligned members oppose the full veil; no legal mandate.

common-currency.rationale: Plebiscito.eu's poll asked whether to adopt the euro and received majority support, and Liga Veneta is pro-Europe historically.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not a stated Venetist position; some pan-Venetian ideas exist.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Independentists seek a state of their own, though autonomists would accept cultural self-government; split but state-aim is central.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Venetists neither treat themselves as a persecuted minority emigrating nor rule it out; they claim self-rule in their own territory, so the question does not map.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Venetists see identity and nationhood, not economic modes, as primary.

ban-cartels.rationale: Anti-trust policy is not documented; Venetist anti-bureaucracy rhetoric and support for competition conflict with small-firm cooperation.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed; Venetists criticise subsidies to the south but have no documented line on rescuing banks or firms.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Venetists resent court rulings blocking referenda, but a general anti-court stance is not documented.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not documented; mild disagreement inferred from centre-right orientation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Venetists favour EU membership, the euro and trade, rejecting autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The movement is pro-EU and export-oriented, but binding trade standards are not in the sources, so it stays neutral.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Mainstream Venetists disavow violence, and accused militants said they were pacifists.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Venetian Republic tradition and democratic orientation point against hereditary titles, though not a stated demand.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The Statute commits the Region to protect the people's history and heritage, and Venetists want Venetian history taught.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Venetists claim self-rule for themselves and thus are unlikely to endorse tutelage over others.

patriotic-education.rationale: Venetists seek to teach Venetian identity and language, but flag-and-anthem loyalty to Italy is rejected; leaning agree for Venetian patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not documented; the centre-right orientation favours it.

public-money-creation.rationale: Plebiscito.eu's poll supports the euro, implying accepting the existing banking system.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Pro-market orientation implies belief in capitalism's adaptability.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Venetists remember the Republic of Venice's Mediterranean empire, but no source calls for modern influence in its former lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: Venetists favour EU, euro and NATO membership, plainly integration.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The 2012 manifesto rejected xenophobic statements, and no source endorses a right to discriminate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Not addressed; Venetists respect constitutional court rulings while challenging them.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Venetists call the 1797 Campo Formio transfer and 1866 annexation illegitimate, which parallels this principle, though they do not state it generally.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Venetian Republic elected its doge and Venetists are democratic, rejecting hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Not addressed; Venetists prefer majority referendum.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not addressed; Venetists contest Italian legitimacy but through legal routes.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Venetists work through regional councils and parliaments, but do not discuss monarchs.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Venetism does not address animal ethics; most members likely accept the general view but no source states it.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; a conventional view is assumed for an agricultural region.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: A duty of the wealthy toward the poor is not discussed; the 2025 platform's solidarity theme is the closest and too weak to infer from.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory view of mass culture is foreign to Venetist sources, so no stance is inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Venetists see Rome's dominance more in fiscal and administrative terms; the theory of cultural hegemony does not appear.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Venetists apply extraction logic to Rome and the south but not to world economy.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices to native-born citizens is not part of the documented platform, which includes immigrant integration.

party-own-road.rationale: Pathways of communist parties are irrelevant to Venetism, though it does insist that Veneto choose its own road from Rome.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Foreign aid policy is not in Venetist sources; the movement's own self-sufficiency theme applies to regions, not poor countries.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not a mainstream Venetist claim beyond an undefined Venetia.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: No Venetist source discusses descendants of pre-colonial peoples ruling settler descendants; the concept does not fit the movement.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; left and right Venetists differ.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Venetists span left and right, with some left-wing Venetists, so no single view on equating fascism and communism is documented.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical debate with no counterpart in Venetist sources, so no position is inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Venetists protected Venetian heritage but some burned a Garibaldi effigy, with Zaia criticising it; no clear line.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-gap programmes are not part of Venetist platforms, and the sources offer no basis for a stance.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed by Venetist platforms; the sources give no basis for a stance.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Venetists want their own forms of self-government within a European framework, but they do not debate Western institutions' universality.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for domestic work is not a Venetist proposal, and the family-oriented and welfare-focused wings give no clear direction.

filial-duty.rationale: Family-oriented Catholic Veneto culture suggests it, but not documented.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service recruitment is not discussed beyond general anti-bureaucracy complaints, so there is no basis to infer a view.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: No Venetist source covers foreign takeovers; the pro-EU and export-oriented outlook clashes with local-ownership protection.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Zaia-wing socially liberal, Catholic wing conservative.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not addressed beyond support for direct votes.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not documented in Venetist platforms; the lowered-tax orientation and welfare-reform focus conflict.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not a Venetist idea; private land ownership dominates.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Regional-council democracy implies parliament approves budgets.

single-official-language.rationale: Venetists want Venetian recognised alongside Italian and regard it as a separate language, rejecting a sole language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not documented; mild opposition inferred from identity politics.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine has no place in Venetist sources; the centre-right orientation may lean against but it is not documented.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Venetist sources have no stance on consumerism, and the business-friendly base and heritage-focused wing conflict.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying by corporations is not a Venetist theme; the movement's populist target is the Roman state and bureaucracy.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Venetists are internationalist toward Europe and the Plebiscito.eu vote drew foreign commentary, but no source addresses NGO funding limits.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Birth-rate policy is not a documented Venetist platform item, though family-oriented Catholic currents might favour it.

residents-only-property.rationale: Identity protection suggests some support for local limits.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not documented; low-tax and low-bureaucracy suggests opposition.

democratic-peace.rationale: No Venetist source discusses theories about democracies and war, so no position is inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not addressed; independentists contest legitimacy of Italian rule.

non-intervention.rationale: Absolute non-intervention is not part of Venetism, whose independence project itself relies on international attention and EU institutions.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is outside Venetist programmes, so no stance is inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not documented, and the 2012 manifesto rejected xenophobia.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Venetists present themselves as anti-bureaucratic and pro-transparency; not directly stated.

local-production.rationale: Localism and heritage emphasis suggests it, but not documented.

informal-organisation.rationale: Venetists organise as parties and committees.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Venetists contest the Italian Constitution but appeal to international self-determination law, so split.

religious-nation.rationale: Venetist identity is defined by history and language, not faith.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism and keeping taxes in Veneto, against funding the south, is a core Venetist demand.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not addressed explicitly but private property is assumed.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not documented; plausible for a reform-minded centre-right regional government.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Venetists do not link women's equality to system change, and the market-friendly orientation points to neutrality.

socialized-care.rationale: Not documented; family orientation suggests opposition.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Venetists promote Venetian language but not purges; Venetian itself is a mixed Romance language.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not a Venetist theme, though they dispute the 1866 annexation, which is a different question.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; the movement seeks self-rule not settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Venetists are not defined by a third-way economics; the catch-all party includes capitalists and left members alike.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Venetists ground claims in the history of the Republic of Venice and annexation, but this is not framed against others now living there.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No source associates Venetism with it; inferred from the movement's mainstream democratic character.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement itself complains of repression.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Venetists complain of being exploited by Rome, so they would reject this.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional theory does not appear in Venetist sources, so none is inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: No Venetist platform covers gender identity, and the liberal and conservative wings of Liga Veneta differ.

assisted-dying.rationale: Liga Veneta under Zaia took liberal end-of-life positions, with 16 of 19 regional councillors backing an assisted-suicide bill.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: A 2012 manifesto rejected the left-right divide, and Venetist parties describe themselves as covering the spectrum.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The 2010 platform called for integration while Lega-aligned wings are hostile; split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Venetists base legitimacy on the people's will, though a Christian-democratic wing exists.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules are not in documented Venetist programmes; the secular and Catholic strands divide.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace-harassment law is not covered in Venetist sources, so there is no basis for a stance.

social-market-economy.rationale: Platforms combine low taxes and reform with welfare and solidarity, and the Christian-democratic 2025 platform fits this model.

rich-first.rationale: The movement says Veneto prosperous region should not subsidise others, so it is partly sympathetic to uneven growth; not stated.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The poll showed majority support for NATO membership.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Venetists complain of taxes and bureaucracy but have no recorded view on IMF-style conditions; pro-EU and fiscal-conservative leanings conflict.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Venetists appeal to legal procedures, constitutional courts and referendums.

racial-franchise.rationale: Not a Venetist position; inferred from mainstream platforms that call for integration.

online-participation.rationale: Plebiscito.eu organised its 2014 independence vote online and elected a provisional parliament online.

open-government-data.rationale: Plausible from the movement's online-voting practice, not stated.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are not a Venetist instrument; referendums are preferred, so no stance is inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Doctrinal reform is outside Venetism; Catholic-leaning and secular strands would not agree.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Venetist sources do not discuss concentration of wealth; the small-business ethos and low-tax stance give no clear lean.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed in any Venetist platform, and the party's liberal and conservative wings differ.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational power-sharing is not discussed, though Venetists want federal arrangements; no direct stance is documented.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Not documented; the 2025 platform stresses solidarity.

term-limits.rationale: Venetists do not take up term limits, and Zaia served several terms as regional president without issue from the party.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is not part of Venetist politics, so no stance can be inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Church office eligibility is outside the movement's concerns, and no source gives a position.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not documented; modern Italian law and the Statute's equality aim suggest it.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not documented; identity emphasis suggests mild opposition.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not a Venetist idea; Veneto's industrial economy relies on IP.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The reward of work versus ownership is not a Venetist theme; the small-owner economy and left wing diverge.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Absolute pacifism is not a Venetist position; the movement disavows aggression but accepts ordinary law on defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Venetism traces the Venetian nation from the Republic of Venice (697-1797) through to today.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The philosophical question is not addressed by Venetist sources, so no position is inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory debates have no place in Venetist platforms, so no position is inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Venetists commemorate Republic of Venice and Manin's 1848 republic, but no source describes a martyr cult for those who die for the nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: A spiritual-war framing of politics is absent from Venetist sources; the Catholic strand is not described that way.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Venetist ties to emigrant communities suggest a cultural homeland role for the diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Zaia defines Venetism as defending heritage, language and literature, while independentists press for a state; split.

god-not-male.rationale: Theological language is outside Venetist programmes, so no position is documented.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist scriptural interpretation is not a Venetist topic, so no stance is inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Some Venetists advocate Venetia combining Veneto, Friuli and parts of Lombardy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Venetists protested prosecutions of their own activists, but accountability of Italian security forces for past abuses is not a stated Venetist issue.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Venetism is a civic and electoral movement with no drilled youth organisations; the movement's pacifist self-image points against them.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Liga Veneta opposes nuclear power plants in Veneto, and a similar local-risk objection would plausibly extend to weapons, but this is inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The poll showed support for NATO membership, which sits with allied bases, while localist sentiment cuts the other way.

independent-unions.rationale: The movement is mostly about autonomy and taxes and never took a stated line on union independence.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The movement spans left and right with a centre-right mainstream and does not address what counts as socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on local self-government and keeping Veneto's resources in Veneto; no stated policy on ownership.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the movement seeks a federal reform of Italy without a stated view on chambers.

municipal-property.rationale: The mainstream is centre-right and pro-market, so community ownership of the means of production is unlikely; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Federalist and sometimes independentist, but the sources do not describe confederal councils with delegates who only coordinate.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; no clear stated position.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; the 2014 Plebiscito questions concerned the euro and EU, not payment privacy.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the anti-Rome, anti-bureaucracy stance and the Statute's focus on the self-government of the people; the principle is not stated.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Social and cultural positions are mixed and the sources do not address spirituality.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The movement seeks self-government that Rome cannot override, via autonomy, the Statute and referendums; inferred from its demands.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement defines the Venetian people by history, language and territory rather than race, and is not violent or racialist in the mainstream.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Venetian history and culture is strong but is framed as cultural rather than racial; adherents would be split on the wording.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: It pursues its aims by referendums and councils, not force; inferred pacific, defensive stance.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Venetists build their claim to nationhood on the Venetian language and history, as the statute and the movement's overview describe, though they stress a regional, not cross-border, nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the movement's civic, pro-referendum character and the statute's reference to the Venetian people as one self-governing body; not stated.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Venetists blame Rome's centralism, not foreign powers, for Veneto's grievances, and they seek European ties.

free-public-college.rationale: The sources record no program on tuition; the movement's focus is fiscal autonomy.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The Liga Veneta platform stresses low taxes and also environmental concerns, so the sources do not settle this.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's emphasis on heritage handed down from the Republic of Venice.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents span left and right and have no common line.

arms-reduction.rationale: The movement is pro-European and non-violent, and Plebiscito.eu's questions raised NATO membership without a rearmament program; mild support inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Venetists criticise Rome's bureaucracy and stress transparency and referendums; inferred, not stated.

capital-controls.rationale: The movement's business base, pro-euro and pro-EU leanings and Plebiscito.eu's euro questions suggest it would keep capital free to move.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Liga Veneta is a legalist movement pursuing aims by referendum and council, so a state monopoly on arms is inferred; the sources do not discuss it.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the movement's non-violent, institutional character and lack of antimilitarist doctrine; not discussed in the sources.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not documented; Liga Veneta draws on small business and workers alike and stresses labour-market flexibility, so it is split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; the movement favours lower taxes yet also welfare reform, so no clear line is inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from the movement's complaint that Veneto's tax money funds Rome's deficits and its low-tax, anti-waste stance.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed; the movement concerns regional fiscal relations with Italy, not global economic rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement seeks autonomy or independence by legal referendum and statute, working within institutions rather than smashing them, though independentists want a new Venetian state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Regional self-government implies freedom to set own policy, but the sources do not discuss a no-blueprint view; wings differ.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; no documented stance on valuing ecosystems as capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Venetism stresses history, language and the Republic's legacy, but its civic-regionalist and pro-European character makes a sacralised nation contested among adherents.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Liga Veneta's low-tax, anti-waste platform and the minor role of student debt in Italy.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Venetists present Veneto as an exploited region whose taxes flow to Rome, an internal-colonial style claim central to the movement.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right, Catholic-influenced mainstream of the Liga Veneta; sources do not discuss human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; no documented position beyond general hostility to Rome-run institutions.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; Venetism is a regional-political cause with no doctrine on religion.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the Liga Veneta's regional and rural base in Veneto, which favours support for local farmers.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is regionalist and pro-European with no stated nuclear position.

workers-own-party.rationale: Venetism cuts across left and right and frames its cause as a regional, cross-class interest, so a separate workers' party is inferred to be disfavoured.

ban-fgm.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the movement's mainstream centre-right and pro-European outlook.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not a Venetist issue; inferred from Italian law and the movement's mainstream outlook, which accepts equal rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Venetists stress Venetian as a distinct language, but the movement did not address naming of languages across regions, so this is left neutral.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the centre-right Liga Veneta mainstream, which accepts regulatory agencies rather than a pure tort regime.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from a movement built on regional and republican institutions, with no role for customary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; adherents span left and right and have no settled position.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the Liga Veneta's centre-right, law-and-order mainstream.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the Liga Veneta's stress on Venetian identity and integration of immigrants.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the centre-right, business-friendly and anti-bureaucracy line of the Liga Veneta mainstream.

voter-id.rationale: The sources do not discuss voter identification; Italian voters already show ID, and adherents have no distinct position.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is mostly secular-regionalist with a Catholic-cultural centre-right base, so adherents are split.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from the movement's reliance on referendums and elections as its route to autonomy, without a stated theory of democracy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from a modern Italian regional movement whose mainstream accepts ordinary social liberties.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the peaceful, referendum-based and online-organised character of the movement, which depends on open internet access.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses tax retention and lower bureaucracy but has no documented stance on replacing welfare with a negative income tax.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal voting and office-holding for women is settled in Italy and implied by the Statute of Veneto's democratic framework; no adherent contests it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from a mainstream with Catholic-cultural roots that does not treat religion as a cause of women's oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are mixed on social issues and the movement's ethnic claims are cultural and historical rather than biological.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed; the Statute's equality principles point one way, but a movement focused on cutting bureaucracy has no stated position on dedicated agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The movement is pro-European and legalist; support for international courts is inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Venetism is largely secular regionalism with mixed social views; literal scripture is not a theme, so mild disagreement is inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The Statute of Veneto commits to equality and a modern regional constitution; the link to guaranteed participation is inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The centre-right Liga Veneta mainstream is unlikely to defend a planned economy; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: The movement favours referendums and direct consultation, as in Plebiscito.eu and the 2017 referendum, so direct election is inferred to be preferred.

national-church-status.rationale: The Veneto tradition is Catholic but Venetism does not campaign for a state church; adherents are split.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Venetists claim self-government for their own distinct nation within or beyond Italy, and the same principle supports autonomy for other minority regions.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The Plebiscito.eu vote and the independence referendum bills rest on letting the inhabitants decide their status.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The Venetian claim is that existing state borders are not final and the Republic's territory preceded them; inferred for colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split.

equal-conscription.rationale: Venetism is a mainstream European regional movement, and equal treatment in any draft is the modern norm; inferred.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Venetists appeal to the Venetian people's distinct history and the legacy of the Republic; a duty to the ancestral land is inferred from that, not stated.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The movement pursues its aims by referendums and councils, not violence, so killing without trial is inferred to be rejected.

close-ties-china.rationale: Venetism is pro-European and the sources do not discuss China; adherents have no documented line, so this is left neutral.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The sources do not discuss kin minorities abroad; the movement focuses on Veneto's own self-government, so no clear line is inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Liga Veneta platforms do not address common ownership of resources or compensation; no inference is possible.

self-ownership.rationale: A centre-right, low-tax mainstream implies support for individual rights over body and labour, inferred from its liberal economic platform.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The Liga Veneta stresses low taxes and keeping Veneto's tax revenue, from which support for cutting everyday taxes is inferred.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Platforms stress welfare and public-service reform without a documented stance on targeting versus universality.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Venetists work through referendums, councils and a regional statute, and the Liga Veneta is itself a party, so bypassing parties is inferred to be rejected.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Anti-bureaucracy, small-business and low-tax platforms imply opposition to special privileges, inferred rather than documented.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The regional statute grounds self-government in the Venetian people and culture, not in a religious community, so denominational politics is inferred to be unwanted.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The movement stresses language and heritage, but nothing documented addresses combining technology with a return to ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Mainstream Italian regional politics accepts equal divorce rights; the sources are silent, so this is an inference.

national-resource-control.rationale: The core grievance is that Rome takes Veneto's revenue, which implies control of resources should sit with the Venetian people; foreign control is inferred to be disfavoured.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right, business-friendly Liga Veneta mainstream; the sources do not address distribution theory.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The sources do not mention such a tax, and the movement's focus is on keeping Veneto's own tax revenue.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The sources describe social positions as mixed and say nothing on racism, so no clear lean is stated.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Adherents are split: the movement contests Rome's authority but pursues its aims by legal referendums, not disobedience.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred: the movement centres on small-business Veneto and says nothing about automating work.

multipolar-world.rationale: The movement is pro-European and autonomist and the sources do not address a multipolar world order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from the market-oriented centre-right mainstream; not discussed in the sources.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Adherents are split since the movement spans left and right; patriotism toward Veneto is not tied to a workers' politics.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: Venetian identity and history are the movement's defining concern, ahead of material class issues.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right mainstream's anti-bureaucracy, pro-market stance; one-party communist rule is alien to it.

missingStatements.text: A region's people should be able to hold a binding referendum on independence from the state.
missingStatements.rationale: Resolution 44/2012, Bill 342/2013 and the Plebiscito.eu vote all sought a referendum on independence or self-determination.

missingStatements.text: A region that pays more in taxes than it receives should keep a larger share of its tax revenue instead of funding poorer regions.
missingStatements.rationale: Fiscal autonomy and complaints about northern taxes funding southern regions are central Venetist grievances.

notes: Left Venetists, autonomists seeking Article 116 devolution and independentists answer differently on independence, and the Liga Veneta's Zaia, Tosi and Salvini-aligned wings differ on social issues and immigration; most such answers here are low-confidence.
